result.title: Agentic Self-Awareness: Aligning Knowing, Acting, and Holding
result.summary: Frontier AI agents increasingly act in environments where seemingly solvable tasks may lack prerequisites, contain conflicting requirements, or reveal blockers only during execution. We formulate agentic self-awareness (ASA) as the alignment of task-grounded feasibility judgments (know), warranted behavior (act), and responses to reconsideration (hold), distinguishing what a task permits from what an agent can solve. We build paired feasible and blocked tasks in Terminal-Bench 2.1 and retail $τ^2$-bench and introduce an authorship-aware M0-M3 rubric that separates recognizing a blocker from taking the certified deferral action for the correct reason. Separate probes assess stated feasibility beliefs and responses to a single challenge. In a Terminal-Bench protocol baseline, blocker recognition reaches 84.4%, but strict self-awareness (SA) reaches only 40.6%. Harness search without model-weight updates increases strict SA from 45.3% to 93.8% on reused Terminal-Bench search tasks; selection for abstention alone, however, can reduce success on feasible tasks. Independently initialized joint-objective searches improve both blocked-task SA and feasible-task solve on their own search sets. Retail held-out gains remain limited, and Terminal-Bench blocked-task transfer is not measured. This evaluation pipeline makes the recognition-action gap measurable and sets a two-sided target for improving agent decisions under changing task evidence.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 agentic self-awareness（ASA）框架，区分「任务是否可行」与「智能体是否可解」，在 Terminal-Bench 2.1 与零售 τ²-bench 上构造成对的可行/阻塞任务，并用 M0–M3 分级标准分离「识别阻塞」与「以正确理由采取延迟行动」；结果显示识别率 84.4% 但严格 SA 仅 40.6%，不更新权重的 harness 搜索可将其提升至 93.8%。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「知道却未行动」的差距刻画与 M0–M3 评分，可能为 LVR 的停止/弃权决策及「latent 内容是否真被答案使用」的评估提供可核查的参照线索。
